title: An empty-string key is renamed to empty_key and steals a real sibling name
rationale: sanitizeKey substitutes the literal name "empty_key" for an empty key. JSON permits "" as an object key, so this is reachable from ordinary input. Paired with a genuine field actually called empty_key - the substitute name is not reserved and not checked for pre-existence in the source.
catchesBugClass: Silent identity substitution: a sanitizer that invents a name inside the user namespace with no returned mapping, no warning, and no exception. Also catches order-dependence.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the null-key branch, because JSON object keys are never null. It also cannot catch a nested empty key colliding across depths, since the collision set is per-map-level.

predicted.detail: Both fields end up under wrong names and the first value now sits under a name the source assigned to the second. Renaming "" is arguably defensible; a substitute that is not reserved, not reported, and resolves in favour of the synthetic name is not.
